topics.label: Introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture within the cancer course and states its learning objectives.

topics.label: The genetic and cellular basis of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations arise and confer advantages that allow susceptible cells to evolve into cancer.

topics.label: Environmental contributions to cancer risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how exposure associations and population patterns inform the balance between environmental causes and chance in cancer development.

topics.label: Infectious causes of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infections can drive cancer, using Burkitt lymphoma as a detailed example.

topics.label: Environmental carcinogens and mechanisms of DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how environmental exposures produce DNA damage that can become cancer-driving mutations.

topics.label: Tumour initiation and promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics distinguish mutational initiation from the growth-promoting conditions that enable initiated cells to form tumours.

topics.label: Biological context and specificity of carcinogen effects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain and consolidate how biological conditions determine whether carcinogen exposure leads to cancer.

topics.label: Methods for investigating carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how evidence is gathered and interpreted to identify carcinogenic exposures despite the limitations of available methods.

topics.label: Closing summary and risk–benefit decisions
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by summarising its conclusions and framing exposure decisions as a balance of risks and benefits.
